title: Galaxy Classification
body:
Galaxies sort into three broad kinds, arranged by Hubble in a tuning-fork diagram that remains
the standard vocabulary.

```
elliptical (E0-E7)   smooth, featureless, little gas, old red stars, little
                     ongoing star formation
spiral (Sa-Sc)       a disc with arms, gas and dust, active star formation,
                     subdivided by how tightly the arms wind
                     barred spirals (SBa-SBc) have a central bar, as the Milky Way does
irregular            no organised structure, often gas rich, frequently the
                     result of an interaction
```

The sequence was originally read as an evolutionary path, which it is not. It classifies
appearance, and the actual evolutionary driver is interaction: two spirals merging produce an
elliptical, so ellipticals are common in dense clusters and spirals are common in the field.

Distance to another galaxy comes from standard candles inside it, using the
[[Inverse-Square Law]] with Cepheid variables or a Type Ia [[Supernova]] whose luminosity
is known. Galaxies cluster into groups, clusters and superclusters, and the motion of galaxies
within a cluster provides a second independent measurement of [[Dark Matter]].
